Erratic

ih-RAT-ik -- stress on the second syllable, RAT. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Erratic is unpredictable or irregular; without a fixed pattern.

The compass needle grew erratic near the iron deposits, swinging wildly with every step.

Worked Example

All spring the weather lurches without warning -- frost on Monday, a heat wave by Thursday, and hail over the weekend.

Weather with no steady pattern, impossible to predict from one day to the next, is erratic. The word describes anything that wanders off any expected course -- schedules, moods, engines, aim.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unpredictable: impossible to foresee or anticipate

inconsistent: not staying the same; uneven

capricious: given to sudden, whimsical changes

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

steady: regular, constant, and even

dependable: reliable; able to be counted on

Where it sits · how wildly the behavior swings — inconsistent → erratic → capricious

inconsistent vs. erratic: Inconsistent is the tamer word -- an inconsistent player has good days and bad days, while an erratic one swings so wildly and unpredictably that no one can guess what the next moment will bring.

capricious vs. erratic: Capricious can outdo even erratic in sheer whimsy: erratic behavior has no pattern, while capricious behavior changes on pure impulse, as if steered by a mood that rewrites the rules mid-game.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — err

Root — err: to wander, to err (Latin errare -- the same root that gives us error)

Suffix — -atic

Suffix — -atic: having the characteristics of (a fuller form of -ic, from Latin -aticus, as in aquatic and lunatic)

Put it together

Put it together: Err ('to wander', from Latin errare -- the same root that gives us error) + -atic (a fuller form of -ic, as in aquatic) spell erratic: something erratic is literally a wanderer -- it strays from the expected path, the fixed schedule, the steady pattern, and you never know where it will drift next.

Use the root in a new word: erroneous

Use the root in a new word: erroneous: The newspaper printed a correction after its erroneous report named the wrong contest winner.

Word Choice

Erratic describes a pattern over time -- erratic driving, erratic behavior, an erratic heartbeat. One strange event is just odd; when the swings keep coming and no one can predict the next one, the pattern is erratic.
